description: Current Drought - U.S. Drought Monitor is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by National Drought Mitigation Center; NOAA, National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration; USDA, U.S. Department of Agriculture. The U.S. Drought Monitor releases a new map every Thursday, highlighting parts of the United States and its territories that are in various stages of drought. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Drought. Assets: Agriculture and Food Supply, Energy and Utilities, Natural Areas and Wildlife, Transportation and Mobility, Water Infrastructure – General. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
